transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

I've been hearing voices that other people can't hear, and I constantly feel like I'm being watched and monitored by people who want to harm me. This has been happening for about two years and two months now, and it has become too overwhelming to handle on my own. That's why I finally decided to come in today.

Have you also had any periods of several days or more when your mood was unusually high or irritable, with much more energy, less need for sleep, or feeling sped up? Or times of several weeks when you felt very depressed or lost interest in things?

No, I've never had times where I felt unusually energetic, irritable, or didn't need to sleep. But I have definitely had long stretches where I completely lost interest in everything and couldn't find any joy in my usual activities.
Did the voices and feeling watched only happen during those depressed periods, or have they also been present when your mood was not depressed?
I'm not really sure about that. I haven't really thought about whether the voices and feeling watched are linked to my mood or those down times. They just seem to be there most of the time.
When you are not feeling depressed, do the voices or feeling watched still continue most of the time?

Yes, they definitely still continue. I have been hearing those voices and feeling watched constantly for the past two years and two months, regardless of my mood. They are always there and don't seem to depend on whether I am feeling depressed or not.
Have the voices or feeling watched ever gone away completely for at least a few weeks, or have they been present continuously most of the time?
No, they have never gone away, not even for a few weeks. They have been present continuously for the entire two years and two months. It has been completely constant without any break.
Have you had any other symptoms like disorganized speech or behavior, or trouble with motivation, emotions, or social functioning over this time?

Yes, I've really struggled with all of that for over two years now. I have no motivation to do anything, I've completely withdrawn from my family, and I find it hard to show emotion or even find the words to speak. It just feels like I'm totally empty inside.

I'm not really sure if that's what I have, as I've never been formally diagnosed with it. I just know that I've been struggling with these voices and the constant feeling of being watched for over two years now. It has just been incredibly hard to live with.

latest_inference.note: Previously the only candidate was Schizophrenia, and the new information strongly supports keeping it as the sole candidate. The patient has continuous auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions for over two years, with negative symptoms and functional decline. There is no history of manic episodes, and the psychotic symptoms are not confined to mood episodes, making schizoaffective disorder, bipolar disorder with psychotic features, and major depressive disorder with psychotic features less likely. The duration and symptom pattern remain most consistent with schizophrenia.

final_diagnosis.reason: Two-plus years of continuous auditory hallucinations and persecutory delusions, with marked negative symptoms (avolition, social withdrawal, flat affect, poverty of speech) and functional decline. Psychotic symptoms are present outside of mood episodes and have never remitted for weeks, arguing against mood disorder with psychotic features or schizoaffective disorder.
